Your First Analysis

This guide walks you through running your first code analysis with RoselineMCP.

Prerequisites

Before starting, ensure you have:

  • RoselineMCP installed and configured
  • A C# solution or project to analyze
  • Basic understanding of diagnostic IDs

Step 1: Analyze a Simple Solution

Let's start with a basic solution analysis:

Using MCP Client

{
  "tool": "analyzeSolution",
  "parameters": {
    "pathOrGit": "/path/to/YourSolution.sln"
  }
}

Understanding the Response

You'll receive a response like:

{
  "solution": "YourSolution.sln",
  "projects": 3,
  "diagnosticSummary": {
    "error": 0,
    "warning": 12,
    "info": 5,
    "hidden": 2
  },
  "topDiagnostics": [
    {
      "project": "YourApp.Core",
      "file": "Services/DataService.cs",
      "line": 45,
      "column": 12,
      "id": "CS0168",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "The variable 'ex' is declared but never used"
    }
  ]
}

Step 2: Filter by Severity

Focus on the most important issues:

{
  "tool": "analyzeSolution",
  "parameters": {
    "pathOrGit": "/path/to/YourSolution.sln",
    "severity": "error",
    "maxDiagnostics": 20
  }
}

This shows only errors, making it easier to identify critical issues.

Step 3: Analyze Specific Projects

Target specific parts of your solution:

{
  "tool": "analyzeSolution",
  "parameters": {
    "pathOrGit": "/path/to/YourSolution.sln",
    "include": "Core",
    "exclude": "Test"
  }
}

This analyzes only projects containing "Core" in the name, excluding test projects.

Step 4: Get Detailed Project Diagnostics

Dive deeper into a specific project:

{
  "tool": "listDiagnostics",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "YourApp.Core",
    "max": 50
  }
}

Response Includes Statistics

{
  "project": "YourApp.Core",
  "totalDiagnostics": 45,
  "stats": {
    "byId": {
      "CS0168": 8,
      "IDE0005": 12,
      "RCS1213": 3
    },
    "bySeverity": {
      "Warning": 23,
      "Info": 22
    }
  },
  "suggestedFixableIds": ["CS0168", "IDE0005", "RCS1213"],
  "diagnostics": [...]
}

Step 5: Preview Fixes

Before applying fixes, always preview them:

{
  "tool": "applyFixes",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "YourApp.Core",
    "ids": ["CS0168"],
    "previewOnly": true
  }
}

Review the Patch

The response includes a unified diff:

--- a/Services/DataService.cs
+++ b/Services/DataService.cs
@@ -42,7 +42,6 @@
     try
     {
         return await GetDataAsync();
     }
     catch (Exception ex)
     {
-        var unused = ex.Message;
         _logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to get data");
         throw;
     }

Step 6: Apply Fixes

Once you're satisfied with the preview:

{
  "tool": "applyFixes",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "YourApp.Core",
    "ids": ["CS0168", "IDE0005"],
    "previewOnly": false
  }
}

Complete Workflow Example

Here's a complete first analysis workflow:

1. Initial Analysis

# Get overview of all issues
analyzeSolution --path /src/MySolution.sln

2. Focus on Errors

# Check for compilation errors
analyzeSolution --path /src/MySolution.sln --severity error

3. List Project Issues

# Get detailed diagnostics for main project
listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core

4. Preview Fixes

# Preview what would be fixed
applyFixes --project MyApp.Core --ids CS0168,IDE0005 --previewOnly

5. Apply Fixes

# Apply the fixes
applyFixes --project MyApp.Core --ids CS0168,IDE0005

Common First-Time Issues

Issue: No Diagnostics Found

Possible Causes:

  • Solution doesn't have analyzers installed
  • Build errors preventing analysis
  • Incorrect path to solution

Solution:

# Verify the solution builds
dotnet build /path/to/solution.sln

# Check for installed analyzers in .csproj
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers" />

Issue: Too Many Diagnostics

Solution: Use filtering to focus:

{
  "severity": "error",
  "maxDiagnostics": 50,
  "exclude": "Test"
}

Issue: Fixes Not Available

Check fixable IDs: Look at the suggestedFixableIds in the response to see which diagnostics can be automatically fixed.

Tips for Beginners

  1. Start Small: Begin with a single project rather than entire solution
  2. Use Preview: Always preview fixes before applying
  3. Fix Incrementally: Fix one diagnostic type at a time
  4. Check Severity: Focus on errors first, then warnings
  5. Read Messages: Diagnostic messages explain the issues
